questions.question: Famous ruler Kanishka belonged to the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kushan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka belonged to the Kushan dynasty__.
 
• The kushan dynasty was founded by Kujūla Kadphises.
 
• Kanishka ruled around the 1st century CE and was the greatest king of the Kushan dynasty.
 
• At the time of Kanishka, kushan rule was spread over the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, Afghanistan, and possibly areas of Central Asia north of the Kashmir region.
 
• He is also remembered as a great patron of Buddhism.
 
• He studied Buddhism under the Buddhist poet Ashvaghosha.
 
• The Fourth Buddhist Council was also convened under his patronage in Kashmir.
 
• That council compiled The Great Commentary on Abhidharma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Kushanas:

 
 
• The first Kushana dynasty was founded by Kujula Kadphises.
 
• Vima Kadphises issued gold coins in India.
 
• Kanishka founded the second Kushana dynasty.
 
• Their capitals were at Peshawar and Mathura.
 
• The most famous Kushana ruler was Kanishka, he was also known as ‘*Second Ashoka*’.
 
• He started an era in 78 AD which is now known as the Saka Era and is used by the Government of India.
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• During his reign, the 4th Buddhist Council was held in Kundalavana, Kashmir where the doctrines of the Mahayana form of Buddhism were finalized.
 
• The last great Kushana ruler was Vasudeva I.
 
• The Kushanas were the first rulers in India to issue gold coins on a wide scale.

questions.question: All executive actions of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Governor.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

Governor:

__
 
• The Governor’s appointment, his powers and everything related to the office of Governor has been discussed under Article 153 to Article 162 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The role of the Governor is quite similar to that of the President of India.
 
• The Governor performs the same duties as of President, but for the State.
 
• Governor stands as the executive head of a State and the working remains the same as of the office of the President of India.
 
• All the executive action of a state government shall be exercised by order in the name of the Governor.
 
• Under the Constitution of India, the governing machinery is the same as that of the Central Government.
 
• It is stated that the Governor has a dual role.
 
 
• He is the constitutional head of the state, bound by the advice of his council of ministers.
 
• He functions as a vital link between the Union Government and the State Government.
 
 
 
• The term of the governor's office is normally 5 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to Article 164 in the Indian Constitution, Governor appoints Chief Minister.
 
• However, the Governor cannot appoint any random person as the Chief Minister but has to follow a provision.
 
• A leader of the party that has got the majority share of votes in the assembly elections, is appointed as the Chief Minister of the state. 

 
• 
 
 
• Article 75:- The PM shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the PM.

 
 
• The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the COM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
 
• A minister who is not a member of the Parliament (either house) for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a minister.
 
 
 
• Article 75 clearly states that the COM is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
• This means that all the ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission.
 
 
 
• Article 75 also contains the principle of individual responsibility.
 
 
• It states that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove a minister even at a time when the COM enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
• However, the President removes a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
 
 
• The council of Ministers comes into existence after the Ministers have taken the oath to their respective offices.

Structure of Indian Union Executive:

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Battle of Buxar was fought in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1764.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought on October 22, 1764 AD.
 
• It was fought between the joint forces of the Nawab Mir Qasim of Bengal, Nawab Sujauddaula of Awadh and the Mughal ruler Shah Alam II and the British.
 
• The United Indian Army was defeated in the Battle of Buxar fought on October 22, 1764.
 
• In 1765, Suja-ud-daulah and Shah Alam signed a treaty with Company Governor Clive in Allahabad.
 
• Under this treaty, the company was given civil rights in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, which authorized the company to collect revenue from these areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ The reasons for battle were:

 
• Mir Qasim wanted to be independent and shifted his capital to Munger Fort from Calcutta. 
 
• These factors fuelled the English to overthrow him and war broke out between Mir Kasim and the Company in 1763.
 
• Participants of the Battle of Buxar were:
 
 
• Mir Qasim – (Administering Bengal in place of Mir Jafar – Nawab of Bengal)
 
• Shuja-Ud-Daulah – Nawab of Awadh (Oudh)
 
• Shah Alam II – Mughal Emperor
 
 

Result of the Battle of Buxar:

 
• Mir Jafar (Nawab of Bengal) handed over districts of Midnapore, Burdwan, and Chittagong to the English for the maintenance of their army.
 
• The English were also permitted duty-free trade in Bengal, except for a duty of two per cent on salt.
 
• Clive made political settlements with Emperor Shah Alam II and Shuja-Ud-Daula of Awadh in the Treaty of Allahabad.

questions.question: Vishu is predominantly celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Vishu.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vishu festival falls on the first day of the Malayali month of Medam, which occurs on either April 14 or 15 on the Gregorian calendar.​
 
• Vishu festival__
 __
 
• It is celebrated in Kerala as the harvest festival and the astrological New Year of the Malayalis.
 
• Vishu indicates the movement of the sun to Aries or the Mesha Rashi and marks the day from which the farmers begin the plowing of land and other agricultural activities.
 
• In Sanskrit, Vishu means equal, which implies the day with an equal number of hours of day and night or the equinox.
 
• The day of Mesha Sankranti or Mesha Sankramam, Vishu is a family festival.
 
• It is a period dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is celebrated by worshipping Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna.
 
• Vishu Kani, Vishu Kaineettam, and Vishubhalam are the three most important aspects of the Vishu celebrations.
 
 
• As per the religious faith of the people on the previous night of the Vishu festival, a Vishu Kani in the prayer room or worship area of the house before the idol of Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna by the eldest lady of the house.
 
• Vishu Kani is regarded as the symbol of good luck and prosperity by all Hindu Malayalis.
 
 
 
• It marks the beginning of the spring season.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Festivals and their importance__:

 
 

 Nuakhai
 
 
 
• It is the harvest festival of Western Odisha.
 
• 'Nua' means new, and 'Khai' means to eat.
 
• The occasion marks the consumption of the first harvested crops and falls on the Bhadraba Shuklapakhya Panchami (tithi)
 
 
 
 

 Gochi
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in the Lahaul Spiti region of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It is celebrated by the members of the households who have been blessed with a child in the last year.
 
• People gather in these houses, and drink liquor called chhang.
 
 
 
 

 Gudi Padva
 
 
 
• It is a spring-time festival that marks the traditional new year for Marathi and Konkani Hindus

questions.question: A nation that has positive net exports enjoys a trade _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** surplus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** A trade surplus means that a nation is exporting more goods and services than it is importing.**
 
• This results in an inflow of foreign currency, which can be used to** pay off debt or invested in the economy.**
 
• Positive net exports also indicate that a nation is competitive in the global market and has a comparative advantage in certain industries. This can lead to increased employment and economic growth.
 
• On the other hand, a trade deficit means that a nation is importing more than it is exporting, resulting in an outflow of currency. This can lead to a decrease in foreign reserves and potentially weaken the national currency.
 
• ** A trade surplus is not always desirable,** as it can lead to trade tensions with other nations and may cause the domestic industry to become too reliant on exports.A trade deficit may not always be a bad thing, as it can help a nation access goods and services that it cannot produce domestically and may stimulate economic growth through increased consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information____ Some additional points on trade surpluses and deficits:__

 
• Balance of Payments: The terms trade surplus and deficit are part of a country's balance of payments, which includes not only trade in goods and services but also capital transfers and financial transactions. While a trade surplus adds to the balance of payments, a deficit subtracts from it.
 
• Economic Performance: A trade surplus is often seen as a sign of economic strength, and a deficit as a sign of weakness. However, this is an oversimplification. For example, a trade deficit can occur during periods of strong economic growth, when a country's businesses and consumers are buying more goods from overseas. Conversely, a trade surplus could occur during an economic downturn, when there is lower domestic demand for foreign goods.
 
• Currency Implications: Trade balances can affect the value of a country's currency in the foreign exchange markets. A sustained trade surplus can put upward pressure on a country's currency value, while a sustained trade deficit can put downward pressure on it.
 
• Impact on Domestic Industries: Constant trade deficits may harm domestic industries as they have to compete with cheaper or better foreign goods. On the other hand, continuous trade surpluses might lead to protectionist policies which can hinder competition and innovation in the long run.
 
• Debt Levels: Countries with large and persistent trade deficits often need to borrow from other countries to finance their deficits. This can increase the country's overall debt levels and make it more vulnerable to economic crises.
 
• Politics and Trade Policy: Trade surpluses and deficits can have significant impacts on politics and the development of trade policies. For instance, countries facing trade deficits may be more inclined to implement protectionist policies, such as tariffs and quotas, to protect domestic industries. On the other hand, those with trade surpluses might face pressure from other nations to open their markets more.

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: The sun is about ________ km away from the earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __150 million km__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The distance between the sun and the earth is 150.82 million km. 
 
• The distance is referred to as one astronomical unit-the distance light travels in about eight and a half minutes.
 
• The distance between the Earth and the Sun varies slightly over the course of the year.
 
• The sun is the nearest star to earth.
 
• It is continuously emitting heat and light. It is the main source of heat and light energy for all planets in our solar system.
 
• In our solar system, the Earth is the only habitable planet.
 
• The existence of life on Earth is attributed to many ideal factors, including the presence of an atmosphere and water, as well as the appropriate distance from the sun.
 
• The earth appears bluish-green from outer space as light from the landmass and water bodies gets reflected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Sun

 
 
• The sun is by far the largest object in our solar system. It contains 99.8 percent of the solar system’s mass and is a hot ball of glowing gases.
 
• The gravity of the Sun holds the Solar system together keeping everything in its orbit.
 
• Planets orbit the sun in oval-shaped paths called ellipses, with the sun slightly off-center of each ellipse. Without the Sun’s energy, there will be no life on earth.
 
 
 
• The Earth
 
 
• The earth is the 3rd nearest planet to the sun, it is the fifth-largest planet.
 
• It is slightly flattened at the poles. Hence, its shape is described as a Geoid.
 
• The Earth has only one moon.
 
• It is known as the Blue Planet.

questions.question: Give an example of means of personal communication.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** telephone service.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Means of personal communication refers to methods of communication that allow individuals to directly interact with each other.**
 
• ** Television **is not a means of personal communication as it is a** one-way broadcast medium** and does not allow for direct interaction between individuals.
 
• ** Computers** can be used for personal communication through various** means such as email, instant messaging, and video conferencing.**
 
• ** Radio is not a means of personal communication **as it is a **one-way broadcast medium **and does not allow for direct interaction between individuals.
 
• **Telephone service i**s a means of personal communication as it allows individuals to** directly interact with each other through voice communication.**
 
• ** Other means of personal communication **include face-to-face conversations**, text messaging, and social media platforms such as Facebook and Twitter.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: Among the given options, _______ is the method of irrigation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a__** canal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** A canal is a method of irrigation that involves the use of artificial waterways to supply water to crops.** This method is widely used in agriculture to irrigate large areas of land.
 
• **Double cropping** is a practice of growing two crops in the same field in a single growing season. This method is used to maximize the use of land and increase crop yield.
 
• ** Ploughing** is a process of turning over the soil to prepare it for planting. This method is used to loosen the soil and remove weeds, making it easier for crops to grow.
 
• Step cultivation is a method of farming that involves the creation of terraced fields on steep slopes. This method is used to prevent soil erosion and conserve water.
 
• It is important to choose the right method of irrigation depending on the type of crop, soil, and climate conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Double cropping:** This practice is common in areas with a long growing season and mild winters, such as the southern United States.
 
• **Ploughing:** This method has been used for centuries and is still widely used today, although modern ploughs are more efficient and require less labor.
 
• **Step cultivation: **This method is commonly used in mountainous regions, such as Southeast Asia and the Andes Mountains in South America.
 
• ** Canal: **Canals can be either natural or artificial and are used to transport water from one place to another. They are commonly used in irrigation systems to supply water to crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Furrow irrigation-

 
 
• Furrow irrigation is a method of laying out the water channels in such a way where gravity plays the role of providing just enough water for suitable plants to grow. It is usually made by the planned placement of ridges and furrows. It is a kind of surface irrigation system.
 
 
 
• Sprinkler irrigation-
 
 
• There is no requirement of using many areas of your field for setting up sprinkler irrigation. The interference with cultivation for setting up the sprinkler irrigation is very less.
 
• Frequent application of water can be supplied to the plants automatically. The water distribution will always be equal.
 
 
 
• Drip Irrigation-
 
 
• It drips water straight into the root zone and also minimizes evaporation. There are some networks that are used to distribute water equally among all the plants. These are valves, pipes, tubing, and emitters.
 
• Due to improper water supply, fertilizers and nutrients cannot reach the roots of every plant. Drip Irrigation system helps it to reach effectively.
 
• Contour farming –
 
• Contour cultivation (contour farming, contour plowing) is a sustainable way of farming where farmers plant crops across or perpendicular to slopes to follow the contours of a slope of a field. This arrangement of plants breaks up the flow of water and makes it harder for soil erosion to occur.
 
• Plowing and planting across slope contours create man-made water breaks that not only allow enough time for the water to enter the soil, but also to settles the topsoil without washing it down the slope.

questions.question: Identify an element that is NOT a semi-metal.

• ** A semi-metal, also known as a metalloid, is an element that has properties of both metals and non-metals. It typically has a shiny appearance, but is brittle and can be a poor conductor of electricity.**
 
• Cesium is a highly reactive alkali metal and is not a semi-metal. It is a soft, silvery-golden alkali metal with a melting point of only 28.5, making it one of the few metals that are liquid at or near room temperature.
 
• The chemical elements known as semimetals or metalloids are those that share characteristics with both metals and nonmetals.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Freshwater:

 
 
• Freshwater is water that contains only minimal quantities of dissolved salts, thus distinguishing it from seawater or brackish water.
 
• All freshwater ultimately comes from precipitation of atmospheric water vapor, reaching inland lakes, rivers, and groundwater bodies directly, or after melting of snow or ice.
 
• Freshwater is vital to life and yet it is a finite resource.
 
• Of all the water on Earth, just 3% is fresh water.
 
• Although critical to natural and human communities, freshwater is threatened by a myriad of forces including overdevelopment, polluted runoff, and global warming.
 
• With this in mind, WWF partners with communities, businesses, and others to decrease pollution, increase water efficiency, and protect natural areas to ensure enough clean water exists to conserve wildlife and provide a healthy future for all.
 
• Water is an amazing element. It is unique because it can be naturally found as a solid, liquid, or gas.
 
• As lakes, oceans, rivers, and streams increase in temperature, some water will change from liquid to gas, collecting together into clouds of moisture.
 
• As these clouds float over cooler seas or land, some of the moisture falls as rain or snow.
 
• Rain and snow that falls on the land either seeps into low places feeding aquifers and groundwater tables or flows downhill, forming headwaters.
 
• These headwaters flow into streams, which in turn flow into rivers or lakes.
 
• Eventually, these waters flow to the sea, starting the cycle over again.

questions.question: Which political leader became Member of Legislative Assembly from Thrikkakara constituency, Kerala in June 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Uma Thomas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Uma Thomas became a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from Thrikkakara constituency, Kerala in June 2022.**
 
• She belongs to the **Indian National Congress (INC) party and won the seat by defeating the incumbent MLA and Communist Party of India (Marxist) candidate P.T. Thomas.**
 
• **Pinarayi Vijayan*** *is the current **Chief Minister of Kerala** and represents the Dharmadom constituency in the state assembly. He was not elected from Thrikkakara constituency in June 2022.
 
• ** Amit Shah** is a national-level politician from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and currently serves as the **Minister of Home Affairs in the Government of India.** He has not contested any assembly elections in Kerala recently.
 
• **Jagdeep Dhankhar** is the Governor of West Bengal and has no connection to the **Kerala assembly elections.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• A Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is a representative, elected by the voters of an electoral district (constituency) to the legislature of the State government in the Indian system of government.
 
• From each constituency, the people elect one representative who then becomes a member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA). 
 
• Each state is divided into a specific number of Assembly constituencies.
 
• In this case, the elected representative is called the Member of the Legislative Assembly or an MLA.
 
• Each Parliamentary constituency has several assembly constituencies.

questions.question: Consumers expect better-quality foods with _______ of nutrients.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** retention.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Nutrient retention is the process of preserving the nutrient content of food during processing, handling, and cooking. It ensures that the food retains its nutritional value and quality.**
 
• Consumers are becoming more health-conscious and are seeking foods that are rich in nutrients. Therefore, food manufacturers are focusing on nutrient retention to meet consumer demand.
 
• Contamination refers to the presence of harmful substances in food, such as bacteria, viruses, and toxins. It can cause foodborne illnesses and pose a risk to public health.
 
• Adulteration involves adding inferior or harmful substances to food to increase its quantity or improve its appearance. It is a fraudulent practice that can deceive consumers and compromise their health.
 
• Exclusion does not relate to the preservation of nutrients in food. It means the act of keeping something or someone out or preventing their participation.

questions.question: Who among the following is a Bharatanatyam performer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanjore Balasaraswati.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Tanjore Balasaraswati was a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer who was known for her impeccable technique and emotive performances. She was born into a family of musicians and dancers and was trained by her mother, who was also a Bharatanatyam dancer.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam has been recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• Bharatanatyam, presumably the oldest classical dance of India is regarded as the mother of many other Indian classical dance forms.
 
• It is indigenous to the Tamil Nadu region and prevalent in southern India.
 
• Its techniques and terminology have been traced back to ancient texts such as the Natya-shastra.
 
• Bharatanatyam was originally performed exclusively by female temple dancers and was not brought to the stage for public performance until about 1930.
 
• Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Padam, Varnam are some of the elements of Bharatanatyam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitara Devi was a Kathak dancer**, not a Bharatanatyam performer.
 
• **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma was a Mohiniyattam performer**, not a Bharatanatyam performer.
 
• **Satyanarayana Sarma is a well-known Kuchipudi dancer,** not a Bharatanatyam performer.
